title: The Day a Wave of Molasses Killed 21 People
description:
In 1919, a giant tank of molasses burst in Boston and sent a wave through the streets faster than people could run. It sounds absurd. Twenty-one people died.

Sources: History.com's account of the January 1919 Great Molasses Flood; the Great Molasses Flood entry and investigation findings.

#shorts #truestory #history

scenes.text: On 15/01/1919 in Boston, a fifty eight foot tall tank holding two and a half million gallons of molasses suddenly gives way.
The bolts blow out like bullets. A wave of molasses twenty five feet high tears through the streets at thirty five miles an hour.
That's faster than most people can run. The wave crushed buildings, swept away train cars, and trapped people and horses in the street.
Twenty one people died. Some were found days later, still stuck in molasses that had hardened like concrete.
A six year investigation followed, with three thousand witnesses. The cause: the tank had been built too fast, too cheap, and never properly tested.
Locals said you could smell molasses in that part of Boston on hot summer days for decades afterward.
